chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

And I heard him saying: 'The tawaf of the Mutamatti' is that he performs circumambulation around the Kaaba, and runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and shortens his hair; so when he does that, he has entered the state of Ihram解除 (Ihram).

key_terms.أَحَلَّ: Ahalla: To become permissible/allowed, referring to exiting the state of Ihram restrictions
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa: One of the two hills between which Sa'i is performed
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: Al-Mutamatti': A pilgrim who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in between
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah: The second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.يَسْعَى: Sa'i: Running/walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual steps that complete Umrah for a Mutamatti pilgrim and allow them to exit the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific sequence of rites that constitute the completion of Umrah for the Mutamatti', emphasizing that the combination of Tawaf, Sa'i, and Qasr (shortening hair) is sufficient to exit the state of Ihram restrictions. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is pivotal in establishing that these three acts are the definitive markers of 'Ihlal', allowing the pilgrim to enjoy lawful pleasures until the start of Hajj days. The emphasis on 'Qasr' rather than full 'Halb' (shaving) highlights the flexibility within the ritual while maintaining the core requirement of physical alteration to signify release from Ihram.
